title: Spot instances and handling the interruption: the discount and its price

videos.script: AWS has machines nobody is using right now. It will rent them to you for much less. {{offer}} The catch is one sentence. When AWS needs a machine back, it takes it, with two minutes' notice. {{notice}} That sounds like a reason to stay away. For a lot of software it is not. A web server behind a load balancer, a worker reading a queue, a build that can run again: each can lose one instance and carry on. {{fits}} This lesson starts with the price, and with why moto's spot prices are not prices at all. Then the two signals AWS sends before it takes an instance, and a small script that listens for them. {{signals}} Then the shape that makes spot safe. A group with a floor of on-demand instances, and the rest on spot, across several instance types. You will write that policy and watch moto store it, and launch something else. {{group}} And last, the question to ask before moving anything to spot. Not how important it is. What one interruption would cost. {{cost}}
